metadata.case_name: Chile vs. Uruguay (Southern Cone consolidation, Mod4 abstention test)
metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Mod4 abstention: the two highest-quality South American democracies. Pre-event P1 gap is Chile 0.759 vs Uruguay 0.652 = 0.107, at/just inside the WGI margin of error -> the framework should ABSTAIN on an intra-pair ordinal ranking rather than confidently rank Chile above Uruguay. Both should remain consolidated (Tier 2).
metadata.notes: Reference-based record (country_ref + years; no embedded indicators). Resolved scores are real MI v2 re-scores. Post-1985/1990 redemocratization -> 2024; scored ~1996 vs 2024. The point of the case is the abstention discipline: the post-period ordering in fact reverses (Uruguay edges above Chile on post-MI), vindicating the refusal to manufacture a confident ranking from a within-margin pre-gap.

pre_event.event_description: A decade into redemocratization (Chile from 1990, Uruguay from 1985), both Southern Cone states had consolidated as the region's two highest-quality democracies with strong rule of law and low corruption relative to Latin American peers.

Chile.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Region-leading rule of law and control of corruption; copper rents present but well below the resource-curse threshold and institutionally managed.

Uruguay.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Region-leading voice/accountability and rule of law; no significant resource rents.

Chile.outcome_summary: Remained consolidated (Tier 2): MI 0.747 -> 0.691, P1 0.759 -> 0.673. Absorbed the 2019-2022 estallido social and a two-cycle constitutional rewrite process (both draft constitutions rejected) entirely through institutional/electoral channels; peaceful turnovers continued (Boric 2022). No breakdown.
key_events: two constitutional-referendum cycles, both rejected, no rupture

Uruguay.outcome_summary: Remained consolidated (Tier 2): MI 0.726 -> 0.716, P1 0.652 -> 0.698. Continued as the region's top-scoring democracy on voice and rule of law; peaceful turnovers (2020, 2024). Post-MI (0.716) in fact edges above Chile's (0.691) -> the pre-period ordinal ranking REVERSED, vindicating the Mod4 abstention.

a_trajectory.evidence: Both stayed Tier 2 (Chile MI 0.747->0.691; Uruguay 0.726->0.716); the intra-pair ordering reversed (Uruguay edged above Chile on post-MI), so any confident pre-period ranking would have been wrong
a_trajectory.explanation: AUTO (V3 consolidated-pair caution): both pre-P1 > 0.6 (min 0.652) and gap 0.107 < high-end margin 0.15 -> abstain; capacity differences don't predict trajectory above the threshold. | prior: AUTO: top mismatch — pred Chile vs outcome Uruguay; gap 0.107. | prior: Mod4 abstention vindicated: the pre-event P1 gap (0.107) was within margin, the framework declined to rank them, and the outcome ordering actually flipped. Coded PARTIAL to mark the abstention rather than a clean ordinal confirmation.

analysis.overall_assessment: A clean Mod4 discipline test: the two best South American democracies stayed consolidated and effectively tied, and the framework correctly abstained on the head-to-head ranking. The post-period order reversed, which would have falsified any confident pre-period ranking -> abstention was not merely cautious, it was correct.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: The strongest available demonstration that Mod4 abstention pays off: a within-margin pre-gap (0.107) preceded an actual ordering REVERSAL, so the discipline of declining to rank near-ties prevented a falsification the framework would otherwise have walked into. Near-ties are genuinely unrankable, not just uncertain.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; reinforces the Mod4 within-margin abstention rule.
